articles.title: Before You Connect an MCP Server: A Dependency Review for Agent Builders
articles.excerpt: Adding an MCP server to an agent takes a few lines of configuration. That convenience hides a real decision: you are giving software you did not write a path into your agent's actions and, often, into…
articles.body: Adding an MCP server to an agent takes a few lines of configuration. That convenience hides a real decision: you are giving software you did not write a path into your agent's actions and, often, into your users' data. We treat every MCP server as a dependency and review it before it reaches production. Here is the review, grounded in what the Model Context Protocol specification actually says. Start with what the spec says about tools The specification does not soften this point: tools represent arbitrary code execution and must be treated with appropriate caution. Servers can also attach annotations that describe how a tool behaves. On those, the spec is just as clear: clients must consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.

articles.title: Idle in transaction in Postgres: why pg_cancel_backend returns true and changes nothing
articles.excerpt: I build HeapDeck, an iPhone and iPad app for Postgres on call. You won't need it here: everything below runs in psql. The API slows down, then a migration hangs, and pg_stat_activity shows a session i…
articles.body: I build HeapDeck , an iPhone and iPad app for Postgres on call. You won't need it here: everything below runs in psql . The API slows down, then a migration hangs, and pg_stat_activity shows a session in idle in transaction with a transaction that started forty minutes ago. It runs nothing and uses no CPU, and the rest of the table's traffic waits on it. You call pg_cancel_backend , Postgres answers t , and the session stays where it was. Reproduce it Open three psql sessions on a scratch database. I ran this on PostgreSQL 18.6.

articles.title: comm -23 Said Nine Camera Clips Were Missing From the Backup. Two Were.
articles.excerpt: I set up a test folder of camera clips and a backup folder with two of them missing, then ran the line a nightly backup check usually rests on, the one that prints what is in one list and not the othe…
articles.body: I set up a test folder of camera clips and a backup folder with two of them missing, then ran the line a nightly backup check usually rests on, the one that prints what is in one list and not the other: comm -23 phone.txt backup.txt . It reported nine missing clips. comm did not hide the problem. It printed a warning and exited with status 1. A job that only wants a number throws both away. Below are the test folders, what comm printed, what the GNU manual says about it, a brute-force check of when comm stays quiet, and the version of the job I would run instead. Disclosure: I make an Android camera app. Nothing below uses its code or describes how it records, names or stores anything. The clips are random bytes made on a Linux machine, and every output is pasted from the scripts shown.

articles.title: Website Analytics for Small Business Sites: A Developer's Guide to the 5 Numbers That Matter
articles.excerpt: For developers, this guide starts with implementation: if you want these five numbers to mean anything, wire up GA4 events properly first. Define a small, consistent event taxonomy, fire a key event f…
articles.body: For developers, this guide starts with implementation: if you want these five numbers to mean anything, wire up GA4 events properly first. Define a small, consistent event taxonomy, fire a key event for each real business action — a form submission, a quote request, a phone tap, a booking — using gtag('event', ...) or your tag manager's data layer, and verify each event in GA4 DebugView before you trust any report. Clean event names, one conversion per action, and a quick test on a phone will save you from the empty reports and inflated numbers that make analytics useless. Most small business owners check their website the way they check a shop window. They look at it, decide it looks fine, and move on. That tells you nothing about whether it is working.

articles.excerpt: Google just got a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Easter egg that transports you back to the 1998 version of the search engine — complete with blue links for results.
articles.body: Google just got a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Easter egg that transports you back to the 1998 version of the search engine — complete with blue links for results. The remake of the Nintendo 64 classic comes out this Thursday, November 5, but you can find the secret on Google now if you type “zelda” into the search bar and press enter. This makes the Master Sword appear in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Click the Master Sword and it gets shoved into its pedestal, an audio effect plays, and the screen distorts to pull you through time. Now you’re back at the old, useful, minimalist Google that showed search results as a series of blue links for people to click on. What you’re seeing is Google from 1998, the year the original Ocarina of Time launched.

articles.title: What is Starshield? A look at SpaceX's military satellite network
articles.excerpt: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them?
articles.body: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them? For more than a week in October 2026, Ukrainian drone operators found their high-speed satellite links shut off. Officials in Kyiv said that terminals for SpaceX ’s Starshield network stopped working at speeds of above 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) from Oct. 14, hampering efforts to conduct defensive operations and intercept Russian drones. Full connectivity was restored on Oct. 24, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The arguments over who did what continue, but the affair highlighted how little is publicly understood about Starshield — what it is, how it relates to Starlink , and how it is operated.

articles.body: Europe is preparing to introduce a new requirement that could change how electric bicycle batteries are tracked, repaired, recycled, and potentially even resold. Starting in February 2027, new e-bike batteries sold in the European Union will be required to carry a digital battery passport, giving each battery its own digital identity and making important information about its origins and characteristics accessible throughout its lifetime. And while the rules are European, their impact could eventually reach American e-bike riders, too. more…

articles.title: 'The Sea God Surveys': Watch Rocket Lab launch Japanese Earth-observing satellite today
articles.excerpt: Rocket Lab will launch its 99th mission to date today (Nov. 2), sending a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite to orbit. Here's how to watch live.
articles.body: Rocket Lab will launch its 99th mission to date today (Nov. 2), and you can watch the action live. An Electron rocket is scheduled to lift off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site today, during a window that opens at 11:41 a.m. EST (1641 GMT; 5:41 a.m. on Nov. 3 local New Zealand time), The mission, which Rocket Lab calls "The Sea God Surveys," will carry an Earth-observing radar satellite for the Japanese company iQPS. You can watch it live via Rocket Lab starting about 30 minutes before launch, and Space.com will carry the company's feed if, as expected, it's made available. The patch for Rocket Lab's "The Sea God Surveys" mission, which is expected to launch on Nov. 2, 2025.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 2 – A… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Long Cloud on Mars Explanation: What’s causing this unusually long cloud on Mars ? Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA ’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft. The featured image is from 2018. The cloud forms only during spring and summer seasons and then only during morning hours.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
